camels.title: Do Camels Store Water in Their Humps? The Answer Surprised Me 🐪
camels.q: Do camels store water in their humps? 🐪
camels.text: Do camels store water in their humps? 🐪 Nope! The hump is fat, up to 80 lb of it. The real water trick: oval red blood cells that keep flowing when a camel dries out. Which animal myth should we bust next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #camel
camels.fc: Fun fact: a very thirsty camel can drink around 100 liters (about 26 gallons) of water in roughly 10 minutes! 🐪💧

bulls.title: Do Bulls Really Hate Red? Scientists Tested It 🐂
bulls.q: Do bulls really hate the color red? 🐂
bulls.text: Do bulls really hate red? 🐂 Surprise: bulls can't even see red the way we do. In tests they charged moving capes of any color – it's the movement that sets them off. Which animal myth fooled you the longest? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #bull
bulls.fc: Fun fact: cattle have only 2 kinds of color cones (we have 3), so a red cape looks like a dull brownish gray to a bull! 🐂

bats.title: Are Bats Really Blind? Not Even Close 🦇
bats.text: Are bats really blind? 🦇 Not at all – every bat species can see! Many fruit bats have sharp night vision, some even see UV light, and insect hunters add echolocation. Night vision or sonar? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #bats
bats.fc: Fun fact: some bats switch between their eyes and echolocation depending on the situation – two senses, one super-navigator! 🦇

goldfish.title: Do Goldfish Really Have a 3-Second Memory? A Lever Proved It Wrong 🐠
goldfish.text: Do goldfish have a 3-second memory? 🐠 Not even close! Goldfish learned to press a lever for food during just one hour a day – and some still remembered months later. What should we teach a goldfish? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #goldfish
goldfish.fc: Fun fact: goldfish can learn sounds and colors, and many recognize the person who feeds them! 🐠

ostriches.title: Do Ostriches Bury Their Heads in the Sand? Here's the Truth 🪶
ostriches.q: Do ostriches bury their heads in the sand?
ostriches.text: Do ostriches bury their heads in the sand? Never – they couldn't breathe! They lower their heads to turn eggs in a ground nest, or lie flat to hide. What animal myth did you believe? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #ostrich
ostriches.fc: Fun fact: when an ostrich can't run, it may press its head and neck flat to the ground and blend in like a bush! 🪶

owls.title: Can Owls Turn Their Heads All the Way Around? Almost! 🦉
owls.q: Can owls turn their heads all the way around? 🦉
owls.text: Can owls turn their heads 360°? 🦉 Almost – the limit is about 270°! Owl eyes are fixed, so they turn the whole head, with 14 neck bones and special blood pools that keep the brain supplied. How far can you turn yours? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #birds #owl
owls.fc: Fun fact: owls have 14 neck vertebrae – twice as many as humans. That's how they look over their own back! 🦉

sunflowers.title: Do Sunflowers Really Follow the Sun? Only When They're Young 🌻
sunflowers.q: Do sunflowers really follow the sun? 🌻
sunflowers.text: Do sunflowers really follow the sun? 🌻 Only young ones! They turn east to west by day and swing back at night, guided by an inner clock. Grown-ups face east for good. Did you know this one? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #nature #didyouknow #mythbusting #sunflowers
sunflowers.fc: Fun fact: in a 2016 study, east-facing sunflower heads warmed up faster in the morning and got about 5x more bee visits! 🐝

porcupines.title: Can Porcupines Shoot Their Quills? Not Even an Inch 🦔
porcupines.text: Can porcupines shoot their quills? 🦔 No! Their ~30,000 quills sit loosely and pop off when touched. Tiny barbs hook into skin. First they warn you: rattle, then tail swing. Would you hug one? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #porcupine
porcupines.fc: Fun fact: a porcupine grows new quills to replace the ones it loses! 🦔

sloths.title: Why Are Sloths So Slow? It's All About Their Food 🦥
sloths.text: Why are sloths so slow? 🦥 They eat leaves with very little energy, and one meal can take weeks to digest. So they save energy everywhere, and algae even turns their fur green! Would you live at sloth speed? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #sloth
sloths.fc: Fun fact: sloths climb down from their tree to poop only about once a week! 🦥

hippos.title: Can Hippos Swim? They Actually Moonwalk Underwater 🦛
hippos.text: Can hippos swim? 🦛 Not really! They are too dense to float, so they walk and bounce along the river bottom and push off to breathe. They can even do it while asleep! Which animal myth next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #hippo
hippos.fc: Fun fact: a hippo can hold its breath for about 5 minutes and surfaces to breathe without waking up! 🦛

pigs.title: Do Pigs Really Sweat a Lot? The Saying Is Wrong 🐷
pigs.q: Do pigs really sweat a lot? 🐷
pigs.text: Do pigs really sweat a lot? 🐷 Not at all! Pigs have hardly any working sweat glands. That's why they love mud: it cools them as it dries and works like sunscreen. Which animal saying should we check next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #pigs
pigs.fc: Fun fact: wet mud keeps a pig cool longer than plain water, because it dries more slowly! 🐷

starfish.title: Is a Starfish Really a Fish? Not Even Close ⭐
starfish.q: Is a starfish really a fish? ⭐
starfish.text: Is a starfish really a fish? ⭐ Nope! No gills, no fins, no backbone. Sea stars are cousins of sea urchins, pump seawater instead of blood, and have an eye on every arm! Did you know this one? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #ocean #didyouknow #mythbusting #seastar
starfish.fc: Fun fact: many sea stars can regrow a lost arm, and some species can even regrow a whole body from one arm! ⭐

bees.title: Do All Bees Die After They Sting? Most Don't 🐝
bees.q: Do all bees die after they sting? 🐝
bees.text: Do all bees die after they sting? 🐝 No! Only honeybee workers, because their barbed stinger gets stuck in our skin. Bumblebees have smooth stingers, and male bees can't sting at all. Which bug myth next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #bees
bees.fc: Fun fact: when a honeybee stings another insect, it can usually pull its stinger out and survive! 🐝
tags: do bees die after they sting

sharks.title: Do Sharks Die If They Stop Swimming? Most Can Take Naps 🦈
sharks.q: Do sharks die if they stop swimming? 🦈

giraffes.title: How Long Do Giraffes Sleep? Less Than You Think 🦒
giraffes.text: How long do giraffes sleep? 🦒 Not long! They mostly doze standing up in short naps – about 4.5 hours a day in zoos. For deep sleep they lie down and rest their head on their body. How long do you sleep? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #giraffe
giraffes.fc: Fun fact: a giraffe's deep sleep often lasts only a few minutes – with its long neck curled back like a pillow! 🦒

bananas.title: Is a Banana a Berry? Botanists Say Yes! 🍌
bananas.text: Is a banana a berry? 🍌 Yes! To botanists it's a true berry: it grows from one flower with one ovary and keeps its seeds inside. Strawberries? Not true berries! Which fruit surprised you most? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #nature #didyouknow #mythbusting #banana
bananas.fc: Fun fact: each little 'seed' on a strawberry is actually a tiny fruit of its own, with a seed inside! 🍓

ducks.title: Does a Duck's Quack Really Not Echo? Scientists Tested It 🦆
ducks.q: Does a duck's quack really not echo? 🦆
ducks.text: Does a duck's quack really not echo? 🦆 Myth! Scientists tested it: the echo is there, but a quack fades out slowly, so the echo blends right in. Did you believe this one? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #duck
ducks.fc: Fun fact: in mallards, only the females make the classic loud quack – males make a quieter, raspy sound! 🦆

greatwall.title: Can You See the Great Wall of China From Space? Astronauts Say No 🚀
greatwall.q: Can you see the Great Wall of China from space? 🚀
greatwall.text: Can you see the Great Wall of China from space? 🚀 Not with the naked eye! It's only about as wide as a road and blends into the land. China's first astronaut couldn't spot it in 2003. Which space myth next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #space #didyouknow #mythbusting #greatwall
greatwall.fc: Fun fact: with zoom lenses, astronauts on the space station have photographed parts of the Great Wall! 📸

moonside.title: Is There a Dark Side of the Moon? It Gets Just as Much Sun 🌙
moonside.q: Is there a dark side of the Moon? 🌙
moonside.text: Is there a dark side of the Moon? 🌙 Not really! The far side gets just as much sunlight. We never see it because the Moon spins once per orbit. At new moon, it's in full sunshine! Which space myth next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #space #didyouknow #mythbusting #moon
moonside.fc: Fun fact: the first photos of the Moon's far side came from the Soviet probe Luna 3 in October 1959! 🌙

leaves.title: Why Do Leaves Change Color in Fall? The Colors Were Hiding 🍁
leaves.q: Why do leaves change color in fall? 🍁
leaves.text: Why do leaves change color in fall? 🍁 Trees stop making green chlorophyll, so the yellow and orange hidden all summer finally show. Many reds are made fresh from trapped sugars. Your favorite fall color? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #nature #didyouknow #goodnews #autumn
leaves.fc: Fun fact: sunny autumn days plus cool (but not freezing) nights make the brightest reds, because more sugar gets trapped in the leaves! 🍂

woodfrogs.title: How Do Wood Frogs Survive Being Frozen? Their Heart Stops! 🐸
woodfrogs.q: How do wood frogs survive being frozen? 🐸
woodfrogs.text: How do wood frogs survive being frozen? 🐸 Their liver floods the body with sugar that works like antifreeze, so ice forms outside the cells. In spring they thaw and hop away! Which animal superpower amazes you most? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #frog
woodfrogs.fc: Fun fact: in Alaska, wood frogs survived around -18 °C (about 0 °F) and stayed frozen for months in the wild! 🐸❄️

geckos.title: How Do Geckos Climb Walls? No Glue Needed 🦎
geckos.text: How do geckos climb walls? 🦎 No glue! Millions of tiny hairs split into billions of tips that get so close to the wall that van der Waals forces make them stick. Which animal trick should we explain next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #gecko
geckos.fc: Fun fact: gecko feet clean themselves as they walk – dirt sticks better to the wall than to the tiny hairs! 🦎

onions.title: Why Do Onions Make Us Cry? It's a Chemical Trap 🧅
onions.q: Why do onions make us cry? 🧅
onions.text: Why do onions make us cry? 🧅 Cutting breaks the onion's cells, two chemicals mix and an enzyme makes an irritating gas. Your eyes flush it out with tears. Tip: chill it first! What makes you cry in the kitchen? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #food #didyouknow #goodnews #onion
onions.fc: Fun fact: the tear gas has a long name – syn-propanethial-S-oxide – and it only forms once the onion is cut! 🧅

squirrels.title: How Do Squirrels Find Their Buried Nuts? They Use a Mental Map 🐿️
squirrels.q: How do squirrels find their buried nuts? 🐿️
squirrels.text: How do squirrels find their buried nuts? 🐿️ They remember spots using landmarks, some even sort nuts by type, and their nose finds the exact place. Forgotten nuts grow into new trees! Seen one digging this fall? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #squirrel
squirrels.fc: Fun fact: in a UC Berkeley study, fox squirrels buried the same kind of nut together – a trick called chunking! 🐿️🌰

catfeet.title: How Do Cats Land on Their Feet? The Twist Explained 🐱
catfeet.q: How do cats land on their feet? 🐱
catfeet.text: How do cats land on their feet? 🐱 The inner ear finds 'up', then the cat twists its front half, then its back half – thanks to a super flexible spine. Falls can still hurt, so keep windows safe! Does your cat love heights? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #cats #goodnews #cat
catfeet.fc: Fun fact: kittens start showing the righting reflex at around 3–4 weeks old and master it by about 7 weeks! 🐱

flamingoleg.title: Why Do Flamingos Stand on One Leg? It's Easier Than Two 🦩
flamingoleg.q: Why do flamingos stand on one leg? 🦩
flamingoleg.text: Why do flamingos stand on one leg? 🦩 It's easier for them: their weight locks the leg joints in place, so they can even nap on one leg using almost no muscle power. Can you stand on one leg for a minute? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #flamingo
flamingoleg.fc: Fun fact: in a 2017 study, even a flamingo body with no muscle activity stayed balanced on one leg – but not on two! 🦩

cateyes.title: Why Do Cats' Eyes Glow in the Dark? They Have a Secret Mirror 🐱
cateyes.q: Why do cats' eyes glow in the dark? 🐱
cateyes.text: Why do cats' eyes glow in the dark? 🐱 Behind the eye sits a shiny mirror layer that bounces light back for a second chance – that's the glow. It helps cats see with about 1/6 of the light we need. Have you seen it? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #cat
cateyes.fc: Fun fact: the mirror layer is called the tapetum lucidum – Latin for "bright carpet"! 🐱✨

earthworms.title: Cut a Worm in Half = Two Worms? Sadly Not 🪱
earthworms.q: Do earthworms become two worms when cut in half? 🪱
earthworms.text: Cut an earthworm in half = two worms? 🪱 Mostly a myth! The front end, with the brain and 5 pairs of hearts, can sometimes regrow a tail – the tail part can't grow a new head. Which superpower would you want? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #earthworm
earthworms.fc: Fun fact: some flatworms called planarians can regrow a whole new body from a tiny piece! 🪱

cows.title: Do Cows Really Have Four Stomachs? Not Quite 🐄
cows.q: Do cows really have four stomachs? 🐄
cows.text: Do cows really have four stomachs? 🐄 Not quite! It's one big stomach with four rooms. The biggest, the rumen, is full of microbes that break down tough grass. Which farm animal should we explain next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #cow
cows.fc: Fun fact: cows burp their food back up and chew it again – "chewing the cud" – for up to 8 hours a day! 🐄

catknead.title: Why Do Cats Knead? It's Actually a Compliment 🐱
catknead.q: Why do cats knead with their paws? 🐱
catknead.text: Why do cats knead? 🐱 Kittens press their mom's belly to help the milk flow – grown cats keep the habit when they feel safe and happy. Scent glands in their paws mark you as theirs! Does your cat make biscuits? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #cats #goodnews #cat
catknead.fc: Fun fact: kneading is so common that cat lovers call it "making biscuits" – it looks like kneading dough! 🐱🍞

ants.title: Can Ants Really Lift 50 Times Their Weight? Even More! 🐜
ants.q: Can ants really lift 50 times their weight? 🐜
ants.text: Can ants lift 50x their weight? 🐜 True! Small animals have strong muscles compared to their tiny weight, and in a lab test an ant's neck held about 5,000x its body weight. Which tiny animal amazes you? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #ant
ants.fc: Fun fact: in a 2014 Ohio State study, an ant's neck joint withstood about 5,000 times the ant's body weight before breaking! 🐜

bears.title: How Do Bears Survive Winter Without Eating? Their Heart Almost Stops 🐻
bears.q: How do bears survive winter without eating? 🐻
bears.text: How do bears survive winter without eating? 🐻 They fatten up in fall, then their heart slows to as few as 8 beats a minute and they burn fat for months. Their body even recycles waste into protein! Sleep all winter? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #bear
bears.fc: Fun fact: mother bears give birth in the den in midwinter – and the tiny cubs nurse while mom keeps sleeping! 🐻

woodpeckers.title: Why Don't Woodpeckers Get Headaches? Scientists Filmed It in Slow Motion 🐦
woodpeckers.text: Why don't woodpeckers get headaches? 🐦 It's not a cushion! Slow-motion videos showed the head hits like a stiff hammer. The real secret: their tiny brains handle the impacts far better than big ones. Which bird next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #birds #goodnews #woodpecker
woodpeckers.fc: Fun fact: woodpeckers can peck up to about 20 times per second – and thousands of times in a single day! 🐦

goosebumps.title: Why Do We Get Goosebumps? A Leftover From Our Furry Past 🥶
goosebumps.text: Why do we get goosebumps? 🥶 Each hair has a tiny muscle that pulls it upright when you're cold or excited. In furry animals that traps warm air – we lost our fur, so we just get bumps! When did you last get them? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #body #didyouknow #goodnews #goosebumps
goosebumps.fc: Fun fact: in a 2020 Harvard study with mice, the same nerves that cause goosebumps also woke up hair-growing stem cells! 🐭

owlflight.title: How Do Owls Fly So Silently? Their Wings Have a Secret 🦉
owlflight.q: How do owls fly so silently? 🦉
owlflight.text: How do owls fly so silently? 🦉 Comb-like teeth on the wing edge break up the rushing air, and velvety feathers soak up sound. Big wings mean fewer flaps! Which animal should we explain next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #owl
owlflight.fc: Fun fact: engineers study owl wings to design quieter fans, wind turbines and aircraft! 🦉✈️

dolphins.title: How Do Dolphins Sleep Without Drowning? Half Their Brain Stays Awake 🐬
dolphins.q: How do dolphins sleep without drowning? 🐬
dolphins.text: How do dolphins sleep without drowning? 🐬 Only one half of the brain sleeps at a time – the other half keeps them breathing and on watch, often with one eye open. Would you sleep like a dolphin? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #dolphin
dolphins.fc: Fun fact: this half-brain sleep is called unihemispheric slow-wave sleep – some birds can do it too! 🐬

popcorn.title: Why Does Popcorn Pop? It's a Tiny Steam Explosion 🍿
popcorn.text: Why does popcorn pop? 🍿 A tiny drop of water inside each kernel turns into steam when heated. The pressure bursts the hard shell and the starch puffs into foam! Team salty or sweet? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #food #didyouknow #goodnews #popcorn
popcorn.fc: Fun fact: high-speed videos showed the pop sound comes from steam escaping, not from the shell cracking! 🍿

polarbears.title: How Do Polar Bears Stay Warm? Their Skin Is Black! 🐻‍❄️
polarbears.q: How do polar bears stay warm in the Arctic? 🐻‍❄️
polarbears.text: How do polar bears stay warm in the Arctic? 🐻‍❄️ Up to 11 cm of fat, two layers of fur and small ears keep the heat in. Surprise: the hairs are see-through and the skin is black! Which cold animal is next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #polarbear
polarbears.fc: Fun fact: polar bears lose so little heat that infrared cameras barely see them – mostly just their breath! 🐻‍❄️
tags: how do polar bears stay warm

seahorses.title: Why Do Male Seahorses Give Birth? Dad Does Everything 🌊
seahorses.q: Why do male seahorses give birth? 🌊
seahorses.text: Why do male seahorses give birth? 🌊 Mom puts her eggs into a pouch on dad's belly. He seals it and feeds the babies oxygen for weeks – then pumps out hundreds of tiny seahorses! Know any other super dads? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #seahorse
seahorses.fc: Fun fact: the pouch grows placenta-like tissue that brings the babies oxygen and nutrients – a true pregnancy! 🌊

butterflies.title: Do Butterflies Really Taste With Their Feet? Yes – Here's Why 🦋
butterflies.q: Do butterflies really taste with their feet? 🦋
butterflies.text: Do butterflies taste with their feet? 🦋 True! Taste sensors on their feet let a mom drum on a leaf to check if it's the right food for her caterpillars before laying eggs. What would you taste with your feet? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #butterfly
butterflies.fc: Fun fact: butterflies drink nectar through a long tube-like tongue called a proboscis that stays coiled up when not in use! 🦋

moonphases.title: Why Does the Moon Change Shape? It Actually Doesn't 🌙
moonphases.q: Why does the Moon change shape? 🌙
moonphases.text: Why does the Moon change shape? 🌙 It doesn't! The Sun always lights half of it. As the Moon circles Earth we see more or less of that bright half – from new moon to full moon. Your favorite phase? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #space #didyouknow #goodnews #moon
moonphases.fc: Fun fact: from one new moon to the next takes about 29.5 days – that's where our word "month" comes from! 🌙

yawning.title: Why Do We Yawn? It's Not About Oxygen 🥱
yawning.text: Why do we yawn? 🥱 Not for oxygen – tests ruled that out. A leading idea: a big yawn may help cool the brain and keep us alert. And yawns spread most between friends and family! Did you just yawn? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #body #didyouknow #goodnews #yawn
yawning.fc: Fun fact: in classic experiments, breathing extra oxygen or extra CO2 didn't change how often people yawned! 🥱

spiderweb.title: Why Don't Spiders Get Stuck in Their Own Webs? 3 Clever Tricks 🕷️
spiderweb.q: Why don't spiders get stuck in their own webs? 🕷️
spiderweb.text: Why don't spiders get stuck in their own webs? 🕷️ The spokes aren't sticky, branching leg hairs barely touch the glue, and a coating on their legs makes it grip less. Plus: careful steps! Spiders: cool or creepy? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #spider
spiderweb.fc: Fun fact: Smithsonian scientists studied orb-weaver spiders in 2012 and found their legs' hairs and coating together beat the glue! 🕷️

twinkle.title: Why Do Stars Twinkle? It's Not the Stars at All ✨
twinkle.text: Why do stars twinkle? ✨ It's our air! Moving layers of warm and cold air bend starlight back and forth. Stars are tiny points, so every wobble shows – planets shine steadier. Ever spotted a planet? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #space #didyouknow #goodnews #stars
twinkle.fc: Fun fact: astronomers call twinkling "scintillation" – and space telescopes avoid it by sitting above the air! 🔭

crickets.title: How Do Crickets Chirp? They Play Their Wings Like a Violin 🦗
crickets.text: How do crickets chirp? 🦗 Not with a voice! A male rubs a scraper on one wing across a ridged file on the other, like a tiny violin. They hear with ears on their front legs! Love the sound or can't sleep? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #cricket
crickets.fc: Fun fact: crickets chirp faster when it's warm – you can even estimate the temperature by counting chirps! 🦗🌡️

stomach.title: Why Does Your Stomach Growl? It's Not Just Hunger 🍽️
stomach.text: Why does your stomach growl? 🍽️ Muscles in your gut squeeze food, gas and liquid along – that bubbling is the sound. When you're empty, cleanup waves sweep through and nothing muffles them! Worst moment yours growled? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #body #didyouknow #goodnews #stomach
stomach.fc: Fun fact: the doctors' word for stomach rumbling is "borborygmi" – it even sounds like a rumble! 🍽️

whiskers.title: What Are Cat Whiskers Really For? They're Built-In Sensors 🐱
whiskers.q: What are cat whiskers really for? 🐱
whiskers.text: What are cat whiskers really for? 🐱 Each whisker sits in a nerve-packed spot and feels the tiniest touch – even moving air. They're about as wide as the body, so cats can test tight gaps. Did you know that? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #cats #goodnews #cat
whiskers.fc: Fun fact: never trim a cat's whiskers – they're sensors, not just decoration, and they help cats move safely in the dark! 🐱

dognose.title: Why Do Dogs Have Wet Noses? It's a Scent Trap 🐶
dognose.q: Why do dogs have wet noses? 🐶
dognose.text: Why do dogs have wet noses? 🐶 A thin layer of mucus traps scent particles, and licking sends the smells to a scent organ in the mouth. A dry nose alone doesn't mean sick! Is your dog's nose wet right now? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #dogs #goodnews #dog
dognose.fc: Fun fact: in a 2020 study, dogs could detect faint heat from warm objects – their cold nose tip may work like a heat sensor! 🐶

snowflakes.title: Why Does Every Snowflake Have Six Sides? It Starts With Water ❄️
snowflakes.q: Why does every snowflake have six sides? ❄️
snowflakes.text: Why does every snowflake have six sides? ❄️ Frozen water molecules link up in a hexagon pattern, and the corners grow fastest into six arms. Each flake takes its own path, so no two are alike! Seen snow yet? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #nature #didyouknow #goodnews #snow
snowflakes.fc: Fun fact: the shape depends on temperature – the classic star-shaped flakes grow best around -15 °C (5 °F)! ❄️
tags: why do snowflakes have six sides

pandas.title: Why Do Pandas Eat So Much Bamboo? Their Gut Wasn't Made for It 🐼
pandas.q: Why do pandas eat so much bamboo? 🐼
pandas.text: Why do pandas eat so much bamboo? 🐼 Pandas have a meat eater's gut and digest less than a fifth of it, so they munch up to 14 hours a day. Bamboo grows all year and few others eat it! Your favorite snack? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #panda
pandas.fc: Fun fact: pandas lost the taste receptor for savory 'umami' flavors – meat doesn't taste as exciting to them! 🐼🎋

kangaroos.title: How Do Kangaroos Hop So Far? Their Legs Work Like Springs 🦘
kangaroos.q: How do kangaroos hop so far? 🦘
kangaroos.text: How do kangaroos hop so far? 🦘 Long tendons stretch like springs on landing and bounce them into the next leap – up to 8 m! Hopping faster barely costs extra energy. Which animal jumps best? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #kangaroo
kangaroos.fc: Fun fact: when kangaroos move slowly, they lean on their strong tail like a fifth leg – scientists call it pentapedal walking! 🦘

frogs.title: Why Do Frogs Croak? They Sing With Their Mouth Shut 🐸
frogs.text: Why do frogs croak? 🐸 Males mostly call to attract a mate. They push air past their vocal cords with their mouth shut, and a balloon-like vocal sac makes it louder. Every species has its own song! Heard frogs at night? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #frog
frogs.fc: Fun fact: the tiny coquí frog of Puerto Rico can call at about 90–100 decibels – roughly as loud as a lawn mower! 🐸

skunks.title: Why Do Skunks Smell So Bad? They Always Warn You First 🦨
skunks.q: Why do skunks smell so bad? 🦨
skunks.text: Why do skunks smell so bad? 🦨 Two glands under the tail make a spray full of sulfur chemicals called thiols. But skunks warn first – hiss, stamp, tail up – and only then spray up to 3 m! Ever smelled one? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #skunk
skunks.fc: Fun fact: spotted skunks do a handstand on their front paws as a final warning before they spray! 🦨

oceansalt.title: Why Is the Ocean Salty? Blame the Rain 🌊
oceansalt.text: Why is the ocean salty? 🌊 Rain slowly wears away rocks, rivers carry the salts to the sea, and the sun lifts the water away – but the salt stays. Over millions of years it built up to about 3.5%. Did you know? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #nature #didyouknow #goodnews #ocean
oceansalt.fc: Fun fact: according to NOAA, the ocean's salt spread over all land would form a layer about 150 m (500 ft) thick! 🌊

koalas.title: Why Do Koalas Sleep So Much? Their Food Is the Reason 🐨
koalas.q: Why do koalas sleep so much? 🐨
koalas.text: Why do koalas sleep so much? 🐨 Eucalyptus leaves are tough, low in energy and full of toxins, so a long gut works for hours to digest them. Resting up to 20 hours a day saves energy! How long do you sleep? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #koala
koalas.fc: Fun fact: on hot days koalas hug the coolest tree trunks to dump body heat – scientists filmed it with thermal cameras! 🐨🌳

pufferfish.title: How Do Pufferfish Puff Up? It's a Water Balloon Trick 🐡
pufferfish.text: How do pufferfish puff up? 🐡 They gulp water into a super stretchy stomach and swell to about 3x their size – too big to swallow! Puffing is exhausting, so they only do it in danger. Which sea animal next? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #goodnews #pufferfish
pufferfish.fc: Fun fact: many pufferfish carry tetrodotoxin – one of nature's strongest poisons – so predators that try once rarely try again! 🐡

mars.title: Why Is Mars Red? The Whole Planet Is Rusty 🔴
mars.text: Why is Mars red? 🔴 Its iron-rich dust and rocks rusted long ago, and dust storms spread that rusty dust everywhere. A 2025 study says the rust formed with water – Mars was once wetter! Would you go? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #space #didyouknow #goodnews #mars
mars.fc: Fun fact: on Mars, sunsets glow blue – the fine dust scatters blue light toward the setting Sun, as NASA rovers photographed! 🌅

fingers.title: Why Do Fingers Get Wrinkly in Water? Your Nerves Do It 🖐️
fingers.q: Why do our fingers get wrinkly in water? 🖐️
fingers.text: Why do fingers get wrinkly in water? 🖐️ Not from soaking! After ~5 minutes your nerves shrink tiny blood vessels and the skin folds. Wrinkly fingers grip wet things better, like tire treads! Did you know? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #body #didyouknow #goodnews #fingers
fingers.fc: Fun fact: in a 2013 Newcastle University study, people with wrinkly fingers moved wet marbles faster than with smooth fingers! 🖐️

penguins.title: Do Penguins Really Have No Knees? The Answer Is Hiding 🐧
penguins.q: Do penguins really have no knees?
penguins.text: Do penguins really have no knees? 🐧 Myth! Every penguin has knees, tucked up inside its body in a deep crouch. The short legs we see are mostly ankle and foot. What surprised you most? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #penguin
penguins.fc: Fun fact: walking costs emperor penguins about twice the energy of other animals their size. Their short legs are built for swimming! 🐧

reindeer.title: Do Reindeer Eyes Really Change Color in Winter? The Arctic Secret 🦌
reindeer.q: Do reindeer eyes really change color in winter?
reindeer.text: Do reindeer eyes really change color in winter? 🦌 Yes! Gold in summer, deep blue in winter. Months of darkness squeeze a mirror layer in the eye, so it turns blue and catches more light. Would you want winter eyes? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #reindeer
reindeer.fc: Fun fact: a blue winter tapetum reflects only about half as much light back out of the eye, so more light stays inside! 🦌

roach.title: Can a Cockroach Live Without Its Head? The Answer Is Creepy 🪳
roach.q: Can a cockroach really live without its head?
roach.text: Can a cockroach really live without its head? 🪳 True! It breathes through tiny holes in its body, and nerve clusters keep it walking for weeks. In the end it can't eat or drink. Would you have guessed? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #cockroach
roach.fc: Fun fact: the cut-off head can keep waving its antennae for hours on its own! 🪳

sharktrees.title: Are Sharks Really Older Than Trees? The Timeline Is Wild 🦈
sharktrees.q: Are sharks really older than trees?
sharktrees.text: Are sharks really older than trees? 🦈 True! Shark scales go back 420 to 450 million years, but the first trees only grew about 385 million years ago. Sharks even outlived the dinosaurs! Did that surprise you? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #shark
sharktrees.fc: Fun fact: the first trees grew around 385 million years ago, long after sharks first swam the seas! 🌳

camelspit.title: Do Camels Really Spit? It's Way Grosser Than You Think 🐪
camelspit.q: Do camels really spit at people?
camelspit.text: Do camels really spit at people? 🐪 Not quite! What flies out is mostly half-digested food from the stomach, mixed with saliva. It's a smelly warning to back off. Would you stand close to a camel? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #camel
camelspit.fc: Fun fact: camels chew cud like cows, bringing food back up from their stomach to chew it again! 🐪

flamingopink.title: Are Flamingos Born Pink? The Answer Surprises Everyone 🦩
flamingopink.text: Are flamingos born pink? 🦩 Myth! Chicks hatch fluffy and gray or white. Their pink comes from carotenoid pigments in the algae and brine shrimp they eat. What color would you be? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #flamingo
flamingopink.fc: Fun fact: it can take a young flamingo about two to three years to get its full pink color! 🦩

hares.title: Do Snowshoe Hares Really Turn White in Winter? The Trick Is Wild 🐇
hares.q: Do snowshoe hares really turn white in winter?
hares.text: Do snowshoe hares really turn white in winter? 🐇 True! Their fur doesn't change color – they grow a whole new white coat, triggered by the shorter days of autumn. Could you spot one in the snow? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #snowshoehare
hares.fc: Fun fact: a snowshoe hare's huge hind feet spread its weight, so it can run on soft snow without sinking! 🐾

zebras.title: Are Zebras White With Black Stripes? Look Under the Fur 🦓
zebras.q: Are zebras white with black stripes?
zebras.text: Are zebras white with black stripes? 🦓 Not quite! Under the fur, a zebra's skin is black. In the white stripes, the hair simply grows without pigment. Did you guess right? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #zebra
zebras.fc: Fun fact: in a 2019 study, far fewer biting flies landed on zebras than on horses – the stripes seem to confuse them! 🦓

octopus.title: Does an Octopus Really Have Three Hearts? It Gets Even Weirder 🐙
octopus.q: Does an octopus really have three hearts?
octopus.text: Does an octopus really have three hearts? 🐙 True! Two small hearts pump blood through the gills, one big heart feeds the body – and their blood is blue. Which fact surprised you most? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #octopus
octopus.fc: Fun fact: octopus blood uses a copper-based protein called hemocyanin, which turns blue when it carries oxygen! 🐙

giraffeneck.title: Does a Giraffe Have More Neck Bones Than You? Count Again 🦒
giraffeneck.q: Does a giraffe have more neck bones than you?
giraffeneck.text: Does a giraffe have more neck bones than you? 🦒 Myth! A giraffe has seven neck bones, exactly like you. Each one is just super long, making a neck of nearly two meters. Did you know that? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #giraffe
giraffeneck.fc: Fun fact: a single giraffe neck bone can be about 25 centimeters long – longer than a pencil! 🦒

goldfishtank.title: Does a Goldfish Only Grow to the Size of Its Tank? Not Like You Think 🐟
goldfishtank.q: Does a goldfish only grow to the size of its tank?
goldfishtank.text: Does a goldfish only grow to the size of its tank? 🐟 Myth! Dirty water, stress and crowding stunt its growth – the fish stays small but isn't healthier. Is a tiny bowl a good home? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #goldfish
goldfishtank.fc: Fun fact: with clean water and plenty of space, common goldfish can grow to about 30 centimeters! 🐟

lightning.title: Does Lightning Never Strike the Same Place Twice? One Building Disagrees ⚡
lightning.q: Does lightning never strike the same place twice?
lightning.text: Does lightning never strike the same place twice? ⚡ Myth! Tall, pointy things get hit again and again – the Empire State Building takes around 20 to 25 strikes a year. Have you ever seen lightning up close? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #weather #didyouknow #mythbusting #lightning
lightning.fc: Fun fact: during one storm, the Empire State Building was struck eight times in just 24 minutes! ⚡

birdtouch.title: Will a Mother Bird Reject a Chick If You Touch It? Here's the Truth 🐦
birdtouch.q: Will a mother bird reject a chick if you touch it?
birdtouch.text: Will a mother bird reject a chick if you touch it? 🐦 Myth! Most birds have a weak sense of smell and recognize their babies by look and sound. Still, watch nests from a distance. Have you ever helped a bird? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #birds
birdtouch.fc: Fun fact: a fledgling hopping on the ground is often just learning to fly – its parents are usually close by, still feeding it! 🐦

ducksfeet.title: Do Ducks Get Cold Feet Standing on Ice? Their Legs Have a Secret 🦆
ducksfeet.q: Do ducks get cold feet standing on ice?
ducksfeet.text: Do ducks get cold feet standing on ice? 🦆 Not really! Warm blood flowing down the leg passes cold blood coming back up and hands over its heat, so the feet stay just above freezing. Would you stand barefoot on ice? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #didyouknow #mythbusting #ducks
ducksfeet.fc: Fun fact: in mallards, only about 5% of their body heat escapes through their feet – thanks to a built-in heat exchanger! 🦆

breath.title: Why Can You See Your Breath When It's Cold? It's Not What You Think 🌬️
breath.q: Why can you see your breath when it's cold?
breath.text: Why can you see your breath when it's cold? 🌬️ It's a tiny cloud! Your warm breath carries invisible water vapor that turns into tiny droplets in cold air. Did you know you could make clouds? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #winter #didyouknow #goodnews #weather
breath.fc: Fun fact: you can't see your breath on a warm day because the air is warm enough to keep the water as invisible vapor! 🌬️

crocotears.title: Do Crocodiles Really Cry While They Eat? Scientists Checked 🐊
crocotears.q: Do crocodiles really cry while they eat?
crocotears.text: Do crocodiles really cry while they eat? 🐊 True! Scientists filmed alligators and caimans tearing up during meals – likely as hissing and huffing push air through their sinuses. Did you think crocodile tears were real? 👇 Follow for more WHY? ✨ #explained #science #animals #mythbusting #crocodile
crocotears.fc: Fun fact: in one study, 5 out of 7 alligators and caimans had tears in their eyes while eating! 🐊
